still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month on the box, and almost nobody pays it.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, and Congress has still not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit. The 2034 expansion came by CMS rule, not statute.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands. Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.
Tirzepatide (Zepbound/Mounjaro) has no US generic, no implant is on the market, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin approved for children aged 6–11.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 33.6% ever-used minus 23.0% current leaves 10.6% of adults who have used the drugs and are off now. About 58% of current users are on a second or later course (13.3 points), and 2.8 points cycled and are off again, so 16.1 / 33.6 ≈ 48% of ever-users have cycled. That leaves 7.8 points who stopped once and never restarted. This fits one-year persistence still near one-third on weekly and oral products, with restart rates pushed toward the top of the 36–47% range by $45 generics and new Medicare/Medicaid coverage. A cycle means a stop of 3+ months. Planned 'drug holidays' of 1–6 weeks are counted separately: ~31% of current users (~19.5M) report a holiday or self-directed dose step-down in the past 12 months. Age check: 0.20×13 + 0.33×21.8 + 0.24×32.5 + 0.23×23.5 = 2.6 + 7.2 + 7.8 + 5.4 = 23.0. Income thirds average 23.0. Users: 23.0% of ~274M adults ≈ 63.0M. Payer mix: Medicare ~16.5M (26%), Medicaid ~6.5M (10%), so public programmes cover ~23.0M (36.5%) and are now the largest payer type. Legitimate cash (generic pharmacy, TrumpRx, direct, telehealth) ~20.5M (33%), including ~0.9M on rebranded calm/'food-noise' plans. Commercial ~15.5M (25%). Imported or counterfeit ~4.0M (6%), down from 7.5M. Total: 16.5 + 6.5 + 20.5 + 15.5 + 4.0 = 63.0M. The bottom third's gain (14 → 19.5) moved from gray vials to generic semaglutide paid by Medicaid or $45 cash. About 4.8M new users since 2032 roughly match the 4.8-point rise in ever-use. Adult obesity is ~32.8%. About 19% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, still concentrated in the rural South and among adults who are uninsured and not on Medicaid in the 10 non-expansion states. Pediatric: ~1.4% of under-18s are on a drug, ~3.1% of 12–17s (up mainly through Medicaid EPSDT coverage of generic semaglutide), and ~0.22% of 6–11s are on liraglutide. About 4.7M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping, and roughly 1 in 3 children live in a household where a parent takes scheduled drug holidays.

access.public_coverage: Under the CMS final rule of April 2033 (effective plan year 2034), incretins prescribed for chronic weight management in adults with BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity, are no longer treated as excludable 'weight loss agents'. Part D plans must cover them, generic semaglutide must be tried first, and branded products need prior authorisation. The same reinterpretation applies to Medicaid, so the 43 states that had excluded these drugs now cover generic semaglutide through state plan amendments filed during 2034. EPSDT extends coverage to adolescents. FICTIONAL arithmetic, Medicare: ~7.0M branded users (tirzepatide on OSA/CV/dementia-risk codes, MariTide, orals, generic-intolerant) × ~$210 net × 12 ≈ $17.6B, plus ~9.5M generic semaglutide users × ~$38 net × 12 ≈ $4.3B. Total ≈ $21.9B gross Part D incretin spend, down from ~$31.6B in 2032 on 5.3M more users, because existing diabetes and CV users were switched to generic. New obesity-benefit users (~5.3M × $38 × 12 ≈ $2.4B) are close to the CMS actuary's $2.6B first-year estimate. The dementia-risk route (~1.9M × $245 × 12 ≈ $5.6B) is unchanged inside the branded total. Medicaid: ~4.5M generic × ~$30 net × 12 ≈ $1.6B, plus ~2.0M branded diabetes-code users × ~$160 × 12 ≈ $3.8B, ≈ $5.4B total, roughly two-thirds federal. The two state Medicaid programmes that tie continuation to adherence and BMI progress kept those criteria as permitted utilisation management.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $3–25 a month, and several of the same firms now hold US ANDAs. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials sell for $20–50 in markets without enforceable patents. Canadian and Brazilian generics have fallen to CAD 40–70 and BRL 150–250. India and China supply roughly two-thirds of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Generic semaglutide injectable entered the US in February 2033 under patent-settlement entry dates, alongside a Novo Nordisk authorised generic. By Q4 2033, seven ANDA holders were selling vials at $45–55 a month cash at big-box and cost-plus pharmacies and prefilled pens at $59–69. Branded TrumpRx prices held: oral starting doses $149, Wegovy pill maintenance $199, Zepbound $249–299. Branded oral semaglutide has no generic because the SNAC formulation patents run later. Orals' share fell from ~46% to ~38% of users as cheap generic injectables pulled cost-sensitive users back to needles. MariTide is ~4.1M users, ~3.4M of them clinic-administered inside employer tracks, which shrank to ~5.0M enrollees as some employers moved tracks to generic semaglutide. Employer coverage rose from 30% to 37%, almost entirely through generic-only tiers. Retatrutide is ~$399 cash direct. Amycretin stays at $1,249 list with prior authorisation. The gray market shrank to ~4.0M users and now consists mainly of tirzepatide/retatrutide analogues and people avoiding prescriptions, adherence records or the new label. Telegram sellers market 'no-label' tirzepatide.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic; generic semaglutide injectable since Feb 2033)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: cardiovascular risk reduction (semaglutide incl. generics; tirzepatide)
adolescent obesity 12+ (semaglutide incl. generics, liraglutide, Wegovy pill)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; growth-monitoring label)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide); the extension to adults without CVD was not approved in this window
mainstream_offlabel_uses: dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD, now often generic semaglutide reimbursed under the Medicare/Medicaid obesity criteria
alcohol reduction via telehealth and EAPs (sNDA received a CRL in Nov 2033)
rebranded 'food-noise' plans (formerly calm/focus), ~0.9M subscribers, now mostly on generic semaglutide or low-dose oral
scheduled drug holidays and self-directed dose step-downs to manage blunting
semaglutide in under-12s with severe obesity (off-label; low and still falling)
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Honouring new_indications: none and next_gen_launch: none. The oral semaglutide AUD sNDA (filed Jan 2032) received a Complete Response Letter in Nov 2033: the FDA asked for prospective psychiatric and reward-function data after Novo's unsealed exploratory reward-scale analyses. Tirzepatide's dementia confirmatory trial read out in Jun 2034 with a modest primary-endpoint benefit, and Lilly resubmitted the non-CVD extension in Nov 2034, with no decision before 2035. The bimagrumab-type lean-mass adjunct (filed Jul 2032) had its review extended after a split advisory committee in May 2034 and is not approved, so no new class launched. Implant programmes remain in phase 2. The only market change in this window is US generic semaglutide injectable, a new source of an existing molecule. Tirzepatide's US composition patents run to the mid-2030s. US branded net prices fell ~8% in 2033–34, faster than trend, under generic and public-formulary pressure. The global incretin market is ~$172B (2033), with volume up sharply and US revenue per user down.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside clinic tracks. New pattern: GI events on restarting after drug holidays (see holiday entry).
Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation centres on EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; EPI MDL ongoing and the source of the 2033 document unsealing.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Hip-fracture HR ~1.3 in users 65+ after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. The fracture exposure is now spread across ~5M new Medicare obesity-benefit users, most without DXA baselines.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained. The CMS rule did not require DXA before Part D obesity coverage; DXA code in use.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the anhedonia analyses, which found blunting without excess suicidality.

FICTIONAL: FDA's postmarketing observational study (Jul 2033) found clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~6.8% of users at maintenance doses vs ~3.1% of matched controls, ~10% on retatrutide and ~4% vs ~3% at low doses. Novo's unsealed pooled exploratory scale data from 2019–2023 trials showed ~5% vs ~2% on placebo. Effects are dose-related and mostly reverse within 2–6 weeks of dose reduction or interruption.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling (Mar 2034) in Warnings and Precautions as 'anhedonia and emotional blunting', with the pooled ~5% vs ~2% figure, dose-reduction advice and a screening question at follow-up. Generic labels carry it. In Apr 2034 FDA warning letters to three telehealth platforms said marketing calm as a benefit promotes a labelled adverse effect.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months. Short holidays produce small rebounds; holidays that stretch into stops behave like discontinuation.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic-therapy framing and continuation criteria in two Medicaid programmes.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users. Low ferritin in adolescent girls.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language on labels, now inherited by generics.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× incidence after 5+ years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years). Tirzepatide's 6-year data show a small excess (HR ~1.3) that is now nominally significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class warning, inherited by generics. Tirzepatide label update under negotiation at end of 2034.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of semaglutide follow-up. Cycling now also includes scheduled holidays, whose long-run effects on bone, pancreas and regain trajectories are uncharacterised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue; FDA asked sponsors for holiday-pattern data in 2034.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~29,000 cumulatively, but the yearly rate fell ~40% as gray users moved to $45 generics. Remaining harms concentrate in tirzepatide/retatrutide analogue vials. Poison-centre calls are ~3.5× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts and CBP seizures continue; no statute changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 36-month liraglutide PMR update (Jan 2034) shows the prepubertal height-velocity deficit holding at ~0.6 cm/year, with partial catch-up in children who stopped. The Swedish registry ARFID HR is ~1.7. Final adult height is still unknown. Adolescent starts under Medicaid EPSDT rose in 2034, often in clinics without paediatric endocrinology.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Monitoring labels (6-monthly growth velocity, Tanner staging, eating-disorder screening) carried onto generics. No age restriction. EMA review concluded with similar monitoring language.

safety_ledger.effect: Holiday re-escalation GI events and erratic dosing
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Poison-centre and ED reports of severe vomiting and dehydration in users who restart at full maintenance dose after 2+ weeks off. ~2,100 ED visits were attributed in a 2034 CDC surveillance note. Most were on cheap generic pens.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA (Aug 2034) asked sponsors and ANDA holders to add re-titration guidance after missed doses beyond two weeks; labelling pending.

food_and_beverage.state: About 41% of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~13% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~11%. The new loss is in the value tier: Dollar General and Kroger's lower-income formats saw value-pack snack volumes drop for the first time as Medicaid and $45 generics reached zip codes that gray vials had served unevenly. Zip-code planograms are being redrawn. Holiday weeks are visible in scanner data as weekend spikes in baking and confectionery.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~15% from 2025 and beer ~10%. Drug holidays created a lumpy pattern of Friday-to-Sunday surges in on-premise sales in Austin and Nashville and weaker weekdays. Midwestern bar closures continue. Non-alcoholic 'calm' drinks lost marketing language after the label change.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat. QSR value menus in Memphis and the Delta lost traffic as regainers got generics. Casual dining added 'off-week' tasting menus and holiday-friendly dessert specials. Portion-tiered menus are standard.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking, but a few small fat-positive brands linked to the backlash grew from a tiny base. Resale and stretch serve cyclers. Mass retailers re-cut size runs in lower-income zip codes as Medicaid users lose weight.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Planet Fitness-type budget chains added Medicare-age 'bone and muscle' classes as new obesity-benefit users arrived. Premium DXA-plus-coaching memberships hold at $250–400 a month. Family strength gyms keep gaining over paediatric weight programmes.

insurance.state: Employer coverage rose to 37% through generic-only tiers. Pharmacy trend eased to ~+3% as generic semaglutide replaced branded fills. Adherence differentials persist under the 2027 guidance. Part D base premium growth slowed for 2035 bids as incretin spend fell. PBMs lost rebate income on semaglutide and pushed MariTide and tirzepatide preference deals harder.

pharma.state: Novo Nordisk's US semaglutide revenue fell by more than half on generic entry, and it carries a ~$900M legal provision, a DOJ civil investigative demand and a new chief medical officer. Lilly grows on tirzepatide and retatrutide, Amgen on MariTide, Boehringer on survodutide. Indian ANDA holders (several of the same firms supplying the Indian domestic market) took most generic semaglutide volume. Counterfeit-defence spending fell.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Body shape still reads as income, but less sharply now that thinness is cheap. Weekly needles and pharmacy-vial bodies show up in Medicare waiting rooms and Medicaid clinics. The status signal moved to texture: visible muscle, a scanned DXA and, newly, evidence of feeling. Being 'full volume' (expressive, hungry, laughing loudly at dinner) is read in Austin and Brooklyn as either off-drug or on holiday, and both have cachet.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Upper-income professionals prize off-drug lean or a 'managed dose' with coach-scheduled holidays. In Memphis, gray-market cyclers became Medicaid generic users within a year, and the cycler's face is starting to soften into the steadier, plain thinness of covered users. Southern retirees on the new Medicare benefit are the fastest-losing group in the country, and the least scanned. Upper-income parents in Bethesda and Plano keep prepubertal children off drugs, while adolescent starts rise in Medicaid families.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter on dosing weeks and longer on holiday weeks. Families plan birthdays, Thanksgiving and weddings around who is 'off', and some churches print holiday-friendly potluck calendars. Bread Alone, now ~900 congregations, pairs fasting with 'feasting Sundays' and frames appetite as a gift the drug takes away.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps dropped 'on a calm plan' tags after the label and added 'holiday weeks'. Couples synchronise holidays before trips and anniversaries. A partner's flatness is now a labelled side effect rather than a purchase, which changed the conversation in therapy rooms: people ask for a dose change, not acceptance.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: After the label and the Novo documents, appetite reads in the upper tier as aliveness rather than noise. Unmuted's 'Full Volume' pledge, MAHA-aligned 'Natural Appetite' groups and a revived fat-acceptance current led by Black women organisers in Atlanta (the 'Whole Plate' collective) share platforms for the first time, though they disagree on whether Medicare should pay for the drug at all. In Medicaid clinics, appetite is still mostly something to get rid of.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Labelled at ~5% vs ~2% on placebo in pooled trials, and ~6.8% vs ~3.1% of controls observationally at maintenance doses: roughly 2.3M excess cases among ~63M users, before dose effects. Retatrutide ~10%. Low-dose ~4% vs ~3%. ~31% of users (~19.5M) report a planned holiday or step-down in the past year, and about half of them name 'feeling flat' as a reason. Calm/food-noise plans fell from ~1.3M to ~0.9M subscribers after the April 2034 warning letters.
interior_life.framing: Now officially a side effect, 'emotional blunting' on the label, and colloquially 'the flat' or 'going grey'. Telehealth platforms renamed calm plans 'food-noise management'. HR dropped 'steadiness'. Clinicians ask a screening question at refill. Unmuted calls the label a confession.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Holiday requests cluster around performance reviews, pitches and client dinners. Salespeople in Charlotte talk of 'going off for Q4'. Employer tracks quietly stopped praising 'steadiness'. The two EEOC ADA charges remain pending, and some employees cite the labelled effect when disputing poor-engagement reviews. Clinic-administered MariTide makes holidays visible to wellness vendors, and some enrollees who skip doses lose premium credit under the 2027 guidance.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoir is now a mainstream genre, and 'holiday' fiction (a week of feeling everything) has followed. Musicians and comics schedule tours on off-weeks, and Detroit's Unmuted off nights became a monthly circuit in 14 cities. Sportsbooks report wagering spikes in holiday weeks and target users with promotions accordingly. Streaming services stopped selling 'calm-plan cohorts' after the warning letters but still model 'low-arousal' viewers.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples' practices report fewer 'parallel lives' complaints and more negotiation over synchronised holidays. Some partners resent holiday weeks as the only times the other is present. Pharmacists field questions about skipping doses before honeymoons.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The Novo hearings drew rare bipartisan anger: Democrats over the suppressed data, MAHA-aligned Republicans over the drug itself. Opponents call the CMS rule 'Medicare sedation'. Supporters note it costs less than the 2032 spending path. A conservative legal foundation's challenge to the rule is pending. No legislature acted. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal agencies acted while legislatures did not. FDA approved generic semaglutide, added class anhedonia labelling, issued real warning letters over calm marketing, sent a CRL on the AUD sNDA and extended the bimagrumab review. CMS reinterpreted the weight-loss exclusion by rule. No state legislature or agency took independent action. Illinois's ban remains the only one, and Congress passed nothing on incretins.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The CMS final rule (Apr 2033, effective 2034) requires Part D and Medicaid coverage of incretins for obesity with generic step therapy. It is not a mandate on individuals or employers. TrumpRx operates on manufacturer prices. The 2027 tri-agency wellness guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Medicare does not condition coverage on adherence. Two state Medicaid programmes keep BMI-progress continuation criteria as utilisation management. Employer tracks still feed clinic records to wellness vendors under consent, and holiday gaps now appear in those records. The FDA asked platforms to stop selling mood-check-in cohorts tied to calm claims; de-identified data sales continue under other labels.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE rules are unchanged, as is the Army recruit oral pilot. DOT has still not ruled on incretin use among commercial drivers, though the anhedonia label prompted a DOT medical review board request for comment in 2034.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Indian firms now supply most US generic semaglutide legally, which reframed US–India talks from mail enforcement to API quality and inspections. Chinese tirzepatide analogues remain the main gray import, and import alerts against named API makers continue. The cash price gap between the US and India narrowed from ~40–50× to ~3–10× for semaglutide.

events.event: FDA approves the first generic semaglutide injectables as patent-settlement entry dates open; Novo launches an authorised generic, and by year-end seven makers sell vials at $45–55 and pens at $59–69 a month in cash

CMS finalises a rule that incretins for chronic weight management are not excludable 'weight loss agents', requiring Part D and Medicaid coverage from 2034 with generic semaglutide first; Medicare users reach ~16.5M and Medicaid ~6.5M by late 2034

Documents unsealed in the EPI multidistrict litigation show Novo Nordisk held a 2029 pooled analysis of exploratory reward-scale data showing dose-related blunting that it classified as non-reportable, and that its medical-affairs grants funded 'food noise' speakers who advised calm-plan platforms; DOJ opens an inquiry, Senate HELP holds hearings, and Novo's chief medical officer resigns

FDA adds class labelling for anhedonia and emotional blunting to all incretins, including generics, at ~5% vs ~2% on placebo, with dose-reduction advice; warning letters to three calm-plan platforms follow in April

Unmuted, the Bread Alone network and Atlanta's Whole Plate collective hold 'Full Volume' weekends in 140 cities; the pledge to 'eat, feel and refuse the flat' passes 2 million signers as MAHA-aligned groups attack the CMS rule as 'Medicare sedation'

An Obesity Medicine Association consensus statement endorses planned dose step-downs and supervised holidays for blunting after a survey finds ~31% of users took one; a CDC note links ~2,100 ED visits to restarting at full dose

open_tensions: Medicare and Medicaid now pay for more users than anyone else, at generic prices, under a CMS rule that Congress never voted on. A legal challenge is pending, a future administration could reverse it, and ~5M new older users are losing weight without DXA baselines in a cohort with a known fracture signal.

The flatness is labelled at ~5–7% and about a third of users manage it with holidays. Holidays bring re-escalation ER visits, lumpy consumer demand, and adherence records that penalise the gaps under the still-standing 2027 premium guidance.

Novo's suppressed reward data is under DOJ inquiry, and plaintiffs are asking what else sits in the files, including paediatric psychiatric analyses. Generic makers inherit a label written partly by litigation.

Adolescent starts are rising fastest through Medicaid EPSDT in clinics without paediatric endocrinology, while children who started before puberty still grow ~0.6 cm a year slower and no one knows their final height.

prose.headline: Forty-Five Dollars and a Warning Label: Medicare Pays, the Box Admits the Flatness, and America Takes Weekends Off
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 almost one American adult in four takes an incretin drug, about sixty-three million people, and one in three has tried one. What changed most in two years was not the share of people on the drugs but who pays and how much. In February 2033 the patent settlements ran out on schedule and generic semaglutide reached pharmacy shelves. By Christmas a month of vials cost forty-five dollars at a warehouse pharmacy. The Wegovy box still says $1,349, and nobody pays it. The starting pill in the government's cash channel is still $149. The cheapest legitimate drug in the country now costs less than the mail-order vials that had carried the poorest third into the market.

The government made itself the largest payer without Congress voting on it. In April 2033 Medicare's administrators issued a rule saying that a drug for chronic obesity is not a 'weight loss agent' under the old exclusion, and that Part D plans and Medicaid must cover it, generic first. The first-year cost estimate was small because the generic is cheap. Medicare now covers about sixteen and a half million users and Medicaid six and a half million. Total Part D spending on these drugs fell even as five million retirees joined, because the old Ozempic patients were moved to the generic. Most of the new retirees on the benefit have never had a bone scan. A conservative legal foundation has sued over the rule. Congress has held hearings and passed nothing.

The hearings were mostly about Novo Nordisk. In June 2033, documents unsealed in the pancreatic-injury litigation showed that the company had pooled questionnaire data from its trials years earlier and found what users had been describing: a dose-related loss of pleasure. It filed the analysis as exploratory. Its medical-affairs grants had paid speakers on 'food noise' who also advised the calm-subscription companies. The chief medical officer resigned and the Justice Department opened an inquiry. In March 2034 the FDA put the effect on every label, including the generics: anhedonia and emotional blunting in about five percent of patients against two on placebo, and more at higher doses. In April it sent warning letters to the platforms that had been selling the effect as calm. The calm plans renamed themselves food-noise plans and lost a third of their subscribers.

What replaced the marketing was a habit. About a third of users took a planned drug holiday or cut their own dose in the past year. Obesity doctors now endorse doing it with supervision. Emergency rooms see the people who restart at full dose and cannot stop vomiting. Bars in Austin and Nashville see the surge on Friday night. Scanner data show cake mix spiking on holiday weekends. Couples book holidays for their anniversaries. Salespeople in Charlotte talk about going off for the fourth quarter. Sportsbooks have noticed the holiday weeks too.

The backlash found a common stage, though not a common platform. In June, Unmuted, the Bread Alone congregations and an Atlanta collective of Black women organisers called Whole Plate held Full Volume weekends in 140 cities. More than two million people have signed the pledge to eat, feel and refuse the flat. MAHA-aligned groups joined them on the label and split from them on the rule, which they call Medicare sedation. Fat-acceptance organisers want the drug available and the shame gone.

In Memphis the gray vials mostly disappeared within a year. The cyclers became Medicaid patients, and their faces are settling into an ordinary thinness. Teenagers in the same clinics are starting generic semaglutide in numbers the paediatric endocrinologists cannot keep up with. Children who started before puberty still grow more than half a centimetre a year more slowly than expected, and no one yet knows their final height. Seen from outside, the country looks steadier. Every few weeks it eats cake.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Harlan wakes at six in Whitehaven, Memphis, and does not take her shot. It is Thursday, her day. The pen sits in the butter compartment of the fridge with the pharmacy sticker on it: semaglutide, generic, Part D, four dollars. Two years ago it was a vial off a Telegram channel that her nephew picked up from a man near the Walgreens. She still has two of them in a shoe box, unopened, and has never asked herself why she keeps them.

She skips this week because Kiara turns nine on Saturday and Denise made the cake recipe her mother made. She wants to taste it the way it tastes.

At the pharmacy counter the young pharmacist reads off his screen. Any loss of interest in things you used to enjoy? Denise says she taught Sunday school for thirty-one years and these days she just goes. He nods and types. He tells her that if she is off more than two weeks she should start back at the low dose. She says it will only be one.

In the afternoon she sits on the porch while the neighbour's radio plays Al Green, and around three something in her chest lifts that she had not noticed was gone. She cries a little, and it embarrasses her.

She licks the bowl. It is sweeter than she remembered, nearly too sweet. She eats a second spoonful to be sure.

At night her sister calls from Jackson about the Full Volume thing at the church. Denise says she might go and might not. She puts the pen back in the butter compartment, behind the eggs.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The cheapest legitimate drug in the country now costs less than the mail-order vials that had carried the poorest third into the market.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the starting world puts Indian generic vials at $4–30 and a 40–50× gap to US cash prices, so gray vials were not dearer than $45 generics. The sentence contradicts the parent state and the world's own account of why users moved.

least_plausible_claims.quote: About 4.8M new users since 2032 roughly match the 4.8-point rise in ever-use.

rationale.badness: On balance this world is somewhat better than 2032 on access and inequality. Premium-credit penalties for dose gaps under the 2027 guidance persist. The harm is now labelled and discussable, which lowers epistemic badness, but about 19.5M users are self-managing blunting with erratic dosing.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Employer coverage rose from 30% to 37%, almost entirely through generic-only tiers.

With $45 cash generics available, the obvious employer response is to stop covering, and no chain explains why they add coverage. The pharmacy-trend and track-shrinkage figures also sit uneasily with it.

least_plausible_claims.quote: In the afternoon she sits on the porch while the neighbour's radio plays Al Green, and around three something in her chest lifts that she had not noticed was gone.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism: she has only just skipped a weekly dose on the same day, and the world says blunting reverses over 2–6 weeks of dose reduction. Relief within hours contradicts the candidate's own pharmacology.

Overall it is a harder society for some groups but not worse than 2032.

It rests on more than a dozen named places and institutions, and daily life has real texture.
